title: 14.5 A 28nm 192.3TFLOPS/W Accurate/Approximate Dual-Mode-Transpose Digital 6T-SRAM CIM Macro for Floating-Point Edge Training and Inference
problem: SRAM CIM macros focus primarily on inference; on-device training requires backpropagation with transposed weights but prior T-CIM designs waste area (separate FF/BP circuits), use low-precision integer formats (accuracy loss), or rely on analog CIM (PVT sensitivity). Fine-tuning accuracy directly impacts user experience.
motivation: On-device training enables real-time model adaptation, power efficiency, and privacy protection vs. cloud training; current CIM designs inadequately support accurate, efficient training workflows requiring both forward and backward passes with high precision.
method: This 28-nanometer design integrates multiply-accumulate circuits directly into SRAM memory, enabling dual-mode-transpose architecture. One mode performs forward passes with weights directly; the other performs backward passes with transposed weights. Floating-point numbers preserve training precision. An optional approximate computing mode trades some accuracy for faster, more efficient operation.
key_novelty: This design builds multiply-accumulate circuits into SRAM memory and reuses a single set for both forward and backward training by switching between normal and transposed weight modes in floating-point format, eliminating separate circuits.
contributions: 28nm 192.3TFLOPS/W digital SRAM CIM for edge training and inference
Dual-mode architecture reusing MAC circuits for FF and BP phases
Floating-point support preserving training accuracy vs. integer-only prior work
Approximate computing mode for speed/efficiency trade-off
primary_theme: dual-mode SRAM CIM for floating-point training and inference
